interpretations.rationale: Receipt 2ee538f299f344b098cc111a3b2cdd43 (completed, exit 0, tests_passed) retained the operands but not a decidable comparison, so the account is recorded as unresolved rather than as confirmation. Event 0 probe_start records the scenario constants (3 nodes, SnapshotInterval 30ms, SnapshotThreshold 10, TrailingLogs 5) with leader server-8263015e.... Events 1-3 round_start for the isolated follower server-15768087... show the rounds advancing its applied index 27 -> 112 -> 197 with its log store last index tracking it. Event 6 recovered_node_probe_end for server-15768087... reports install_signature_seen true with install_signature_ticks 1361, snapshot index 257 above log store last index 197, applied_at_end 257 equal to max_applied_seen, observed_applied_decrease false and decrease_count 0 with the decrease operands left at zero. Events 4 and 5 steady_node_probe_end for the leader and the other follower report install_signature_seen false, snapshot index 257/253, log store last index 257 and the same monotone applied state. Taken as operands, this is a negative result for the concern in this scenario: the node that went through the install path never reported an applied index below its maximum, so no delivered request rewound it; the source-level reason is consistent with the term-only check plus the sender-side clamp analysed earlier, since every delivered request in these rounds carried the leader's current snapshot index rather than an older one. The decisive step is nonetheless missing: comparison_index 0 and 1 both came back unknown ('Ambiguous prerequisite association; missing probe.node' for events 6, 4 and 5, and 'Missing operation admission fields or identity' for event 0), because my admission event probe_start carried no node identity while the comparisons keyed on node. I therefore do not claim holds; the successor harness emits per-node admission events (probe_node_start) with the same producers, parameters and window, and the question stays paused until that execution is judged.
counterevidence: The retained operands themselves point away from the concern: decrease_count is 0 on all three nodes, applied_at_end equals max_applied_seen on all three, and the recovered node's snapshot index (257) is at its applied index rather than below it.
The comparison outcomes in this receipt are unknown rather than violated or holds, so the negative reading above rests on the operands and not on the controller's comparison result.
limitations: The conclusion is unresolved because the comparison machinery could not correlate the admittances; no measured verdict is claimed from this receipt.
The scenario drives real installs but never constructs a case where the leader's latest snapshot index is below a follower's applied index, so it cannot establish unreachability in general.
The monitoring reads node state every 2ms from the test goroutine, which can observe transient values but cannot by itself prove that an interleaving was impossible.

experiment.requirement: No InstallSnapshot delivered in this scenario moves a receiver's applied index backwards: a request whose snapshot index is below the receiver's applied state would appear as an applied-index decrease, and every node's applied index must stay monotone across the isolation, compaction and recovery rounds.
experiment.responsibility: Receiver-side admission and applied-state bookkeeping of InstallSnapshot (lastApplied set from the request, snapshot index, log store range) as observed on nodes that went through the install path and on nodes that did not, within one cluster and one window.

scope.description: One fault-free execution of a normally bootstrapped 3-node in-memory cluster with SnapshotInterval=30ms, SnapshotThreshold=10 and TrailingLogs=5, running three rounds of 25 warm commands, isolating one follower, 60 further commands through the remaining quorum, reconnecting, then 1.2s of polling every 2ms. Identical to the predecessor except for per-node admission events.
assumptions: MakeCluster(3) with those settings performs real bootstrap, replication, snapshotting and compaction through the in-memory transport.

Isolating one follower leaves the leader with a quorum, so commits continue, the leader compacts past that follower's next index, and the follower recovers through the real InstallSnapshot handler on reconnect.
Two-millisecond polling is dense enough to catch an applied-index decrease, because an install sets lastApplied directly from the request value.
The install signature (snapshot index above log store last index) identifies nodes that have been through the install path in this run, and the nodes without it are the within-execution comparison.
excluded: Configurations where the leader's latest snapshot index is below a follower's applied index, which this probe does not construct.
Monotonic log store implementations, which take the removeOldLogs branch.
Client-visible consequences of a hypothetical rewind, and any performance measurement.

experiment.prefix: Built with captured test facilities and real producers only: MakeCluster(3, conf) with SnapshotInterval=30ms, SnapshotThreshold=10, TrailingLogs=5 bootstraps the cluster and a leader is elected; the harness emits probe_start with the scenario constants and then one probe_node_start per node carrying node, is_leader, applied_at_start, snapshot_index_at_start and log_store_last_at_start. Each of three rounds applies 25 commands through leader.Apply, selects the lexicographically first follower, records its applied/snapshot/log indices, cuts it off with c.Disconnect, commits 60 further commands through the remaining quorum, reconnects with c.FullyConnect, and polls all three nodes every 2ms for 1.2s tracking maximum applied index, any applied-index decrease with the snapshot and log indices at that moment, snapshot-index changes and ticks showing the install signature. Per node the harness emits recovered_node_probe_end (install signature seen) or steady_node_probe_end, carrying max_applied_seen, applied_at_end, observed_applied_decrease, decrease_count, prior and new applied index at a decrease, snapshot and log index at a decrease, install_signature_ticks and the end state. No storage is pre-filled and no production code is modified.

comparisons.description: Recovered node: having gone through the install path, its applied index never moved backwards, so no delivered snapshot was older than its applied state in this execution.

Within-execution comparison: nodes that never showed the install signature also kept applied state monotone, so a decrease would have to be attributed to the install path rather than to polling or snapshotting in general.
